source_text: Visio prima: Factum est in anno quo mortuus est Ozias rex, vidi Dominum sedentem super solium excelsum. Quamdiu Ozias vixit, videre non potuit Isaias — Ozias peccator ingressus templum lepra in fronte. Talem principem animae oportet mori ut visionem Dei videamus. Si Ozias vivit, non videmus gloriam Dei; si moritur, videmus. Non regnet peccatum in mortali corpore — amantes voluptatem magis quam Deum.
pass_a_gloss: Vision first: It-happened in year which dead is Uzziah king, I-saw Lord sitting upon throne high. As-long-as Uzziah lived, to-see not could Isaiah — Uzziah sinner having-entered temple leprosy on forehead. Such prince of-soul it-behooves to-die that vision of-God we-may-see. If Uzziah lives, not we-see glory of-God; if he-dies, we-see. Not let-reign sin in mortal body — loving pleasure more than God.
pass_b_english: First vision: [[In the year King Uzziah died I saw the Lord seated on a high throne >> Bible:Isaiah 6:1]]. As long as Uzziah lived Isaiah could not see — Uzziah the sinner who entered the temple and was [[struck with leprosy on the forehead >> Bible:2 Chronicles 26:16-21]]. Such a prince of the soul must die if we are to see God’s vision. If Uzziah lives we do not see God’s glory; when he dies we see. [[Let not sin reign in your mortal body >> Bible:Romans 6:12]] — those [[loving pleasure rather than God >> Bible:2 Timothy 3:4]].
notes: True OET; no Scheck FOTC Isaiah/Ezekiel.
